images.caption: The Alcázar of Seville is a historic palace of Muslim origin with Christian additions. The Gallery of Grotesques is notable for its fine reliefs and Renaissance decoration, which blend fantastical and animal motifs. The Gardens of the Ladies offer a landscaped space with fountains, orange trees, and elegant walkways, seamlessly integrating nature and architecture. Both elements reflect the artistic richness and splendor of the palace. They exemplify Mudéjar and Renaissance styles, showcasing the Alcázar's evolution over the centuries.

images.caption:
The Alcázar of Seville (Spanish "Reales Alcázares de Sevilla" or "Royal Alcazars of Seville") is a royal palace in Seville, Spain, originally a Moorish fort. The Almohades were the first to build a palace, which was called Al-Muwarak, on the site of the modern day Alcázar. The palace is one of the best remaining examples of mudéjar architecture. Subsequent monarchs have added their own additions to the Alcázar. The upper levels of the Alcázar are still used by the royal family as the official Seville residence and are administered by the Patrimonio Nacional.
